Rashi on Shabbat 52b:10:1.hebrew: שחולקין - יש חילוק בהלכותיהן, ואיני יודע מהו חילוקן:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:10:1.english: That one distinguishes - There is a distinction in their laws, and I do not know what their distinction is.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:10:2.hebrew: אלא לענין שבת - לענין הוצאת שבת, יש חילוק בין יש עליה חותם לשאין עליה חותם, כדאמר לקמן בפ' במה אשה (שבת דף נט.):
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:10:2.english: Only with regard to Shabbat - With regard to carrying out on Shabbat, there is a distinction between [a ring that] has a seal upon it and [one that] does not have a seal upon it, as it says later in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Ishah (Shabbat 59a).

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:10:3.english: This and that are one - All rings have one [and the same] law.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:11:1.english: When he said to him, too - [that] this and that are one [and the same].

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:12:1.hebrew: שהתקינה לחגור בה מתניו - שקבעה בראש רצועה, ועשאה כמין בוקלא (אבזם) שעושין לסרגין של סוסין:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:12:1.english: That he fashioned it to gird his waist with it - That he affixed it to the end of a strap, and made it like a sort of bocle (a buckle) that they make for the saddles of horses.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:12:2.hebrew: ולקשור בה בין כתפיו - בתי זרועותיו, בראצייר"א:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:12:2.english: And to tie with it between his shoulders - [That is, to tie] his sleeves; [in Old French:] braciere.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:12:3.hebrew: טהורה - דהדר הויא לה כטבעת כלים, ולא דמיא לאדם מושך בהם, שאינו משתמש בה כלום, אלא מונחת ועומדת לרצועה. ומיהו, עם הרצועה מקבלת טומאה; אבל אם היה נוטלה ומחזירה — אינה מקבלת טומאה לעצמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:12:3.english: [Is] ritually pure - For it has reverted to being like a ring of utensils, and it is not comparable to [the case where] a person pulls [the animal] with them, for he does not make any use of it; rather, it is merely in place and designated for the strap. Nevertheless, together with the strap it contracts ritual impurity; but if he would remove it and replace it, it does not contract ritual impurity on its own.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:12:4.english: [It was regarding a ring] of a finger [that] he was saying to him - And with regard to Shabbat, there is a distinction.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:13:1.english: Almog - Almug wood, and it is beautiful.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:13:2.hebrew: טמאה - דבתר טבעת אזלינן, ופשוטי כלי מתכות טמאים:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:13:2.english: [It is] ritually impure - For we follow the ring, and flat metal utensils are susceptible to ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:13:3.english: [If] it is of coral, [it is] ritually pure - For it is [in the category of] flat wooden vessels.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:14:1.hebrew: אלא לענין שבת - לענין הוצאת שבת, יש חילוק בין נקובה לשאינו נקובה: דנקובה קתני חייב חטאת, ובשאינה נקובה — כגון אישפיגל"א, שהיא תכשיט — קתני אינו חייב חטאת, בפרק במה אשה (שבת דף נז:):
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:14:1.english: Only with regard to Shabbat - With regard to carrying on Shabbat, there is a distinction between [a needle] with an eye and [one] without an eye: for regarding [a needle] with an eye, [the Mishnah] teaches [that one is] liable to bring a sin-offering; and regarding [one] without an eye — such as an espingle [pin], which is an ornament — [the Mishnah] teaches [that one is] not liable to bring a sin-offering, in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Isha (Shabbat 57b).

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:15:2.english: Its point - Pointe [Old French for a needlepoint].

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:16:2.hebrew: והוא שרישומה - של מחט ניכר, דהוי כלי, וטמאה. ל"א: שרישומה של חלודה ניכר בבגד — היינו עיכוב תפירה, וטהורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:16:2.english: And that is when its mark - [That the mark] of the needle is discernible, so that it is [considered] a vessel, and [thus] it is ritually impure. Another explanation: That the mark of the rust is discernible on the garment — this is [considered] an inhibition of sewing, and [thus] it is ritually pure.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:16:3.hebrew: בשיפא - נישופת בשופינא, שקורין לימ"א (פצירה), שאין בה חלודה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:16:3.english: Regarding a smoothed [needle] - [A needle that was] smoothed with a file, which is called lime (a file), so that it has no rust on it.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:17:1.hebrew: מותר לטלטלה בשבת - בחצר, דהא חזיא ליטול את הקוץ, ותורת כלי עליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:17:1.english: It is permitted to move it on Shabbat - In a courtyard, for it is fit to remove a thorn, and it has the status of a utensil:

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:17:2.hebrew: ולא אמרו נקובה - חלוקה להלכותיה אלא לענין טומאה בלבד, דנקובה מקבלת טומאה, ושאינה נקובה לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:17:2.english: And they did not say “perforated” - [meaning, that it is] differentiated in its laws except with regard to ritual impurity alone, for a perforated [needle] contracts ritual impurity, and one that is not perforated does not.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:18:1.english: Didn’t Abaye interpret it - In the chapter [entitled] Kol HaKelim.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:18:2.hebrew: בגלמי - שהוא גולם, שנקצצה מן החוט ועומדת לינקב. התם הוא דכל זמן שלא נקבה אינה מקבלת טומאה, דהא לא נגמרת מלאכתה, ולענין טומאה "כלי מעשה" כתיב (במדבר ל״א:נ״א) — שגמר כל מעשהו. ומיהו, לענין שבת שריא, דזימנין דממליך עלה ומנח לה הכי, ומשוי לה מנא לנטילת קוץ. אבל מחט שנגמרה מלאכתה, כגון אישפינגל"א, שאינה עומדת לינקב — דא ודא אחת היא לטומאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:18:2.english: With unfinished [needles] - That it is a blank, which was cut from the wire and is destined to be perforated. There [specifically], as long as it has not been perforated, it does not contract ritual impurity, for its manufacture has not been completed, and with regard to ritual impurity, “an article of workmanship” is written (Numbers 31:51) — [meaning] that all of its manufacture has been completed. However, with regard to Shabbat, it is permitted [to move it], for sometimes one reconsiders concerning it and leaves it as is, and designates it as a utensil for removing a thorn. But a needle whose manufacture has been completed, such as a pin [espingle], which is not destined to be perforated — this and that are one and the same with regard to ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:1.hebrew: מרדעת - בשטי"ל. ומניחין אותו כל היום על החמור לחממו, דאמרי אינשי: חמרא, אפילו בתקופת תמוז קריר ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:1.english: A saddlecloth - Bastel [packsaddle]. And they leave it on the donkey all day to warm it, as people say: A donkey, even in the season of Tammuz, feels cold.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:2.english: When it is tied to it - It is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:4.english: Levuvin, sheḥuzot, kevulot, and kevunot - [These are] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:5.hebrew: צרורות - דדיהן צרורות. פעמים ליבש — שמהדקן כדי שלא יחלבו עוד ויתעברו, או יהו שמנות לאכול; ופעמים לחלב — לשמור חלבן שלא יטפטף לארץ, וקושרין להם כיס בדדיהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:5.english: Bound - Their udders are bound. Sometimes [it is] to dry [them] up — for one binds them tightly so that they will no longer produce milk and will conceive, or will become fat for eating; and sometimes [it is] for milk — to preserve their milk so that it does not drip to the ground, and they tie a pouch over their udders.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:6.hebrew: ר' יוסי אוסר בכולן - דמשוי הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:6.english: Rabbi Yosei prohibits with all of them - For it is a burden.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:7.hebrew: חוץ מן הרחלים הכבונות - שהוא שמירת צמרן שלא יטנף, והוי להו תכשיט:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:19:7.english: Except for the ewes that are kevunot - For this is the protection of their wool so that it does not become soiled, and it is [considered] an ornament for them.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:1:1.hebrew: טהורות - דלאו משום תכשיט מיטמאו, דאין תכשיט לכלי, וכלי נמי לא הוו, אלא תכשיט כלי. ומיהו, בעודן מחוברות לכלי, מיטמו עם הכלי, דהוי יד לכלי, דכל המחובר לו הרי הוא כמוהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:1:1.english: Are ritually pure - For they do not contract ritual impurity as ornaments, for there is no [category of] ornament for a utensil, and they are also not utensils [in their own right], but rather [merely] an ornament of a utensil. However, while they are attached to the utensil, they contract ritual impurity along with the utensil, for it is [considered] a handle to the utensil, as whatever is attached to it is like it.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:20:1.hebrew: יוצאות צרורות ליבש - ר' יהודה סבירא ליה כתנא קמא דלאו משוי הוא. ומיהו, ליבש — דמיהדק שפיר, וליכא למיחש דילמא נפיל ואתי לאיתויי; אבל ליחלב — דלא מיהדק שפיר, חיישינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:20:1.english: [Goats] may go out bound to dry - Rabbi Yehuda holds like the First Tanna that it is not a burden. However, [he permits it when bound] to dry [their milk], since it is fastened well and there is no concern lest it fall off and [the owner] come to carry it; but [when bound] to be milked, since it is not fastened well, we are concerned [lest it fall and he carry it].

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:2:1.hebrew: בבאין מנוי אדם לנוי בהמה - מתני', כגון שנעשה שיר זה לתכשיט אדם, ובעודו לאדם נטמא, ולאחר טומאתו נתנו לבהמה, וצריך להטבילו מטומאתו ראשונה, שלא יגע בטהרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:2:1.english: [When] they come from a person’s adornment to an animal’s adornment - [Our] mishna [is dealing with a case] such as where this chain was made for a person’s adornment, and while it was [designated] for a person it contracted ritual impurity, and after its [contraction of] impurity he placed it on an animal; and he must immerse it from its first impurity, so that it will not touch ritually pure items.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:3:1.english: Since a person pulls the animal with them - He considers it a utensil for human use.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:3:2.hebrew: מקל של בהמה - שרודין בו את הגמל או את הנאקה; אי נמי, כעין שעושין להנהיג את הדוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:3:2.english: An animal’s stick - [One] with which they drive a camel or a female camel; or alternatively, like that which they make to lead a bear.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:3:3.hebrew: של מתכת - דאילו של עץ, פשוטי כלי עץ לא מקבלי טומאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:3:3.english: Of metal - For if [it were] of wood, flat wooden utensils do not contract ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:3:4.english: What is the reason - [Why does the Gemara ask this regarding the baraita's ruling? Because] behold, it is [used] for the needs of an animal [and utensils made for animals do not contract ritual impurity].

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:4:1.hebrew: והאיכא חציצה - שטבעת הקבוע בשיר קבוע בו בחוזק, ואין המים נכנסין שם:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:4:1.english: And isn't there an interposition - For the ring attached to the chain is fixed to it tightly, and the water does not enter there.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:5:1.hebrew: בשריתכן - הכה בפטיש, עד שנתפשט ונתרחק הנקב סביב סביב:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:5:1.english: Where he struck them - He struck [them] with a hammer, until the opening expanded and drew away all around.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:6:1.hebrew: כרב יוסף סבירא ליה - דאמר: כשהן של בהמה נמי מקבלי טומאה, הואיל ואדם מושך בהן. הלכך, כי ריתכן לאחר טומאה, אכתי במילתייהו קיימי ולא פרחה טומאתן, דאכתי חזו לבהמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:6:1.english: [He] holds in accordance with Rav Yosef - Who said that when they belong to an animal they also contract ritual impurity, since a person pulls [the animal] with them. Therefore, when he hammered them after [they contracted] impurity, they still remain in their [prior] state and their impurity did not depart, for they are still fit for an animal.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:6:2.hebrew: דאי כרבי יצחק - דאמר: לא מקבל טומאה אלא בעודן לאדם — טומאה זו שקבלו בעודן לאדם, כיון דריתכן ושוב אין נאים לאדם, בטלי להו מתורת תכשיט, וטהרו מטומאתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:6:2.english: As, if [he held] in accordance with Rabbi Yitzḥak - Who said [that chains] contract ritual impurity only while they are [designated] for a person — this impurity that they contracted while they were [designated] for a person, since he welded them and they are no longer suitable for a person, their status as an ornament is nullified, and they are purified from their ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:7:1.hebrew: יורדין לידי טומאתן במחשבה - מאחר שחישב עליו שיניחנו כמות שהוא עכשיו, ולא יוסיף תיקון אחר — הוא גמר מלאכתן, ומקבל טומאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:7:1.english: Descend into their [state of] ritual impurity by means of thought - Since he intended regarding it to leave it as it is now, and not add another improvement, that is the completion of their work, and it [can] contract ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:7:2.hebrew: ואין עולין מטומאתן - מאחר שחישב על העור לעשות שטיח, ירד לידי טומאה. ואם חזר וחישב עליו לרצועו' וסנדלים — לא בטל מתורת כלי, ולא טהר בכך, עד שיתן בו אזמל, דהוי שינוי מעשה. הא בשינוי מעשה מיהא, עולה מטומאתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:7:2.english: And they do not ascend from their ritual impurity - Once one intended concerning the hide to make a mat, it descended into [susceptibility to] ritual impurity. And if he reconsidered and intended it for straps and sandals, it does not lose its status as a vessel and is not purified thereby, until he applies a knife to it, which constitutes an action that effects a change. Thus, through an action that effects a change at least, it ascends from its ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:8:1.english: To improve [it] - And this is its improvement for the needs of an animal.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:8:2.english: Is not an action - To nullify [it] from the status of a utensil.

Rashi on Shabbat 52b:9:1.hebrew: במחוללין - מתחלה נעשו חלולין רחבים, שיש חלל בדביקתן, שנתן טבעת בתוך טבעת כמות שהוא רחב:
Rashi on Shabbat 52b:9:1.english: With spaced [rings] - From the outset they were made hollow [and] wide, so that there is space where they join, as he placed ring within ring while it was wide.

Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:12:1.hebrew: טבעת שהתקינה לחגור בה מתניו - נראה לר"י, דהיינו לחגור מלבושיו שהן רחבים, ואוגדם כנגד מתניו בטבעת — כעין שפי' בקונטרס "לקשור בה את כתפיו":
Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:12:1.english: "A ring that one fashioned to gird his waist with it" - It appears to the Ri that this means to gird his garments, which are wide, and he gathers them at his waist with a ring, similar to what the Kunteres explained [regarding] "to tie with it his shoulders."

Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:13:1.hebrew: היא של אלמוג וחותמה של מתכת - וא"ת: והא יש בה בית קיבול, מקום מושב החותם? וי"ל: דאין זה בית קיבול, דאמרינן: בית קיבול העשוי למלאות — לא שמיה בית קבול:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:13:1.english: "It is of coral and its seal is of metal" - And if you say: But doesn't it have a receptacle, [namely,] the place where the seal is set? And one can say: This is not [considered] a receptacle, as we say: A receptacle that is made to be filled is not called a receptacle.

Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:17:1.hebrew: והתניא מחט בין נקובה בין אינה נקוב' - נראה לר"י, דלא פריך אליב' דאביי — דאיהו הוה מפרש "שאינה נקובה" היינו שניטל חורה או עוקצה — אלא אליב' דרבא פריך, דלדידיה לא מצינן לפרש הכי, כדמוכח בריש כל הכלים (לקמן שבת קכג.). ותימה לר"י, דכיון דלא ידע המקשה דמיירי בגלמי, א"כ בלאו הכי תקשה ליה לרבא, כדפריך בריש כל הכלים (ג"ז שם):
Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:17:1.english: "Wasn't it taught [in a baraita]: A needle, whether it has an eye or does not have an eye" - It appears to the Ri that [the Gemara] is not raising the objection according to [the opinion of] Abaye, for he would interpret [that] "one that does not have an eye" means that its eye or its point was removed; rather, it is raising the objection according to [the opinion of] Rava, for according to him we cannot interpret [it] this way, as is proven at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] "Kol HaKelim" (below, Shabbat 123a). And it is surprising to the Ri, for since the questioner did not know that [the baraita] is dealing with unfinished [needles], if so, even without this [issue], let it be difficult for Rava, as [the Gemara] objects at the beginning of "Kol HaKelim" (ibid.).

Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:2:1.hebrew: בבאין מנוי אדם לנוי בהמה - פירש"י: ובעודו לאדם נטמא. ובחנם פירש כך, דאפילו אחר שיחדו לבהמה מקבל טומאה, שאינו עולה מלקבל טומאה מכאן ואילך אלא בשינוי מעשה, כדמוכח בפ"ק דסוכה (דף יג:) גבי קוצר לאכילה ונמלך לסיכוך. ורש"י בעצמו פירש כן בריש במה אשה (לקמן שבת נח:). וכופת שאור שיחדו לישיבה דאמר טהור — אור"י דמיירי כשיש שינוי מעשה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:2:1.english: When they come from human adornment to animal adornment - Rashi explained: And while it was [still designated] for a person, it became ritually impure. But he explained this without need, for even after one designated it for an animal, it [still] contracts ritual impurity, for it does not cease from being susceptible to ritual impurity from that point on except through an act of alteration, as is proven in the first chapter of Sukkah (13b) regarding one who harvests for food and reconsiders [using it] for sekhakh. And Rashi himself explained so at the beginning of [the chapter] "Bameh Ishah" (below, Shabbat 58b). And [as for] a block of sourdough that one designated for sitting, where [the Gemara] states [that it is] pure — the Ri says that it is dealing with [a case] where there is an act of alteration.

Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:4:1.hebrew: והא איכא חציצה - פירש בקונטרס: שטבעת תקוע בשיר בחוזק, ואין המים נכנסים שם. ואומר ר"י, דצריך לומר שפעמים מסירים אותן ועושים מהן מלאכה בפני עצמן — שאם כל שעה היו קבועים בצואר הבהמה, היה הכל חשיב כלי אחד ולא הוי חציצה. וה"ר פור"ת פירש: "והא איכא חציצה" — לפי שהוא דבוק בצואר הבהמה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:4:1.english: "Isn't there an interposition?" - The Kuntres explained that the ring is tightly jammed into the chain, and the water does not enter there. And the Ri says that one must say that they sometimes remove them [the rings] and perform work with them on their own — for if they were permanently fixed around the animal’s neck, the whole thing would be considered a single utensil and would not be an interposition. And Rabbeinu Porat explained: "Isn't there an interposition?" — because it is pressed against the animal’s neck.

Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:5:1.hebrew: בשריתכן - להכי לא מוקי לה במחוללין, דאין דרך השיר להיות כן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52b:5:1.english: "Where he welded them" - That is why he does not establish it [as referring to links that are] hollowed out, for it is not the way of a chain to be so.
